bihar_raw_news.title: NHAI Allocates ₹50 Crore For Wildlife Conservation Along Varanasi-Kolkata Expressway
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / India / Trending / NHAI Allocates ₹50 Crore For Wildlife Conservation Along Varanasi-Kolkata Expressway NHAI has rolled out a wildlife conservation and environmental protection plan along the Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Expressway in Bihar. by Tanvi Shrivastava Updated: October 18, 2026 12:04 PM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Wikimedia Commons The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has allocated around ₹50 crore to Bihar’s Environment, Forest and Climate Change Department to implement an environmental conservation and wildlife mitigation plan along the Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Expressway. The plan aims to protect wildlife habitats, conserve endangered species and improve road safety while supporting connectivity to key religious and tourist destinations, including Bodh Gaya in Gaya district and the Sun Temple at Deo in neighbouring Aurangabad district. Scroll down to know more. NHAI Provides 50 Crore For Wildlife Range Along Varanasi-Kolkata Expressway According to Times of India, the plan covers wildlife habitat improvement, the conservation of selected Schedule I species, soil and water conservation, forest fire management, and monitoring and evaluation. The initiative also includes planting around 45,000 saplings along the expressway corridor. NHAI’s regional office in Patna organised a media tour on Friday to showcase the project’s progress, engineering features and regional significance. Project director Devendra Kumar Bansal told the portal that the 33-km Package VII, being constructed in Bihar’s Gaya district at a cost of ₹1,248 crore, has achieved around 36% physical progress. The stretch runs from Anarban Saleya village to Sangrampur, covering the section between kilometre 151 and kilometre 184. The package is being developed under the Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM). The wildlife conservation plan has been prepared in coordination with the state forest department and the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI). The package includes two elephant underpasses and two animal overpasses to allow wildlife to cross the expressway safely. These structures, along with other mitigation measures, are designed to reduce disruptions to animal movement and improve road safety. Also Read: Video: Mysore Palace Sees Tourist Jam In Long Weekend; Netizens: & Some Still Stuck On Highway& Expressway To Feature Cameras And Trauma Centres To Boost Road Safety The expressway will also feature high-quality cameras installed at one-kilometre intervals to support monitoring and safety. Trauma centres are planned every 30 km to provide timely medical assistance to passengers in case of emergencies. The Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Expressway will begin at Rivasa in Uttar Pradesh’s Varanasi district and pass through Chandauli in Uttar Pradesh before entering Bihar. It will traverse Kaimur, Rohtas, Aurangabad and Gaya districts, followed by several districts in Jharkhand, including Chatra, Hazaribag, Ranchi, Bokaro, Dhanbad and Ramgarh. Also Read: How India Is Using AI To Find Accident-Prone Highway Stretches Before They Turn Deadly The route will then pass through Purulia and Bankura in West Bengal before connecting to Kolkata. Along with improving regional connectivity, the project is intended to provide better access to important religious and tourist destinations while incorporating measures to protect wildlife and the environment. bihar_raw_news.title: Madhya Pradesh's 1,200 MW Solar-Battery Projects Await Government Nod, Delhi, Haryana ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): Haryana, Delhi and Bihar have agreed to 1,200 MW solar and battery storage projects with Madhya Pradesh. Approval for these projects is pending at the state government level. Once approved and operational, the projects will provide Madhya Pradesh with additional electricity during evening hours, when power demand is at its peak. Sources in the new and renewable energy department said the proposed projects include 500 MW each in partnership with Delhi and Haryana and 200 MW with Bihar. As far as projects with Haryana, Delhi and Bihar are concerned, the generated power will be used by the partner states on a rotational basis. Madhya Pradesh will draw power from October till April, the period during which power demand remains higher. On the other hand, Haryana, Delhi and Bihar would draw power from April till September. Apart from this, Mandsaur's pumped storage project is nearing completion. Its capacity is 1,920 MW. At least 10 more similar projects are in the pipeline in different parts of the state. Projects can be set up in one or two years Additional Chief Secretary for the New and Renewable Energy Department Manu Shrivastava said, We can set up projects within one or two years and supply inexpensive power once the energy department is willing to purchase it. Solar power cheaper than thermal energy The power produced by solar projects is far cheaper than the energy produced by thermal projects. The solar energy rate is Rs 2.15 per unit in comparison to Rs 6 per unit of thermal energy. The installation period for a thermal power plant is at least six years, while solar projects hardly need 12-18 months for their installation. This means that through solar power projects, power generation starts much earlier in comparison to thermal power projects. national_raw_news.title: Protests over rising living costs, low wages and housing prices sweep Belgium, France, Italy and ...
national_raw_news.content: Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across Belgium, France, Italy and Portugal to protest against rising living costs, low wages and the growing difficulty of accessing affordable housing. The demonstrations have put governments across the European Union under pressure. France witnessed widespread unrest, with more than five lakh fifty thousand people participating in demonstrations, according to the Interior Ministry. The protests, which followed weeks of student demonstrations, escalated into clashes, widespread looting and arson as groups of masked protesters targeted shops, historic public buildings and police vehicles. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said around 1,200 people had been arrested and 150 police officers injured. Dozens of shops were looted in several cities, including Paris, Marseille, Nice, Bordeaux and Toulouse. In Limoges, a fire set by masked protesters largely destroyed the historic town hall. Municipal buildings in Marseille and Lille were vandalised, while a tourist office in Lyon was set ablaze. French President Emmanuel Macron vowed that those responsible would be prosecuted. In Belgium, police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in Brussels and Liège following reports of projectiles being thrown at officers and fires being set. Meanwhile, tens of thousands of people reportedly marched in Portugal’s capital, Lisbon, protesting against rising living costs, low wages and soaring housing prices. Portuguese Parliamentary Affairs Minister Carlos Abreu Amorim said the government would not yield to pressure from street demonstrations, while protesters accused political leaders of being out of touch with their concerns. In Italy, demonstrations in Milan against wars and rising living costs turned violent, with protesters clashing with police, looting shops and setting fire to barricades. Police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse the crowds. According to the LaPresse news agency, at least two police officers were injured and around 50 demonstrators were detained. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence, saying that while demonstrating was a right, setting cities ablaze was unacceptable. Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala also said that although the protesters’ concerns were understandable, violence against police and damage to public property could not be justified. Clashes were also reported in Bologna, where some demonstrators allegedly threw stones at police.

national_raw_news.content: In West Bengal, 19 people lost their lives and 25 others were injured in a stampede at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata last evening. The incident occurred at around 8 PM, during the Maha Saptami celebrations. According to media reports, heavy rain and a sudden rush of visitors led to chaos at the crowded pandal. Several people reportedly fell amid the rush, triggering a stampede-like situation. The injured were rushed to Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, R-G Kar Medical College and Hospital, and N-R-S Medical College and Hospital for treatment. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, the state Health Minister and senior government officials visited the hospitals to assess the situation and review the treatment being provided to the injured. The Chief Minister also announced compensation of 25 lakh rupees and a Group D government job for the family of each deceased person. Later, speaking to reporters, the Chief Minister said police have detained the Durga Puja organisers, private security guards and staff on duty for questioning. Describing the incident as tragic, Mr Adhikari said the administration’s immediate priority was to ensure proper medical treatment for the injured. He said, preliminary reports suggest that an announcement made over the loudspeaker by the puja organisers triggered a sudden rush among visitors, leading to the stampede. The Chief Minister announced that a Special Investigation Team, or SIT, headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta High Court, will investigate the stampede at the Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata. The SIT will include members of the Special Task Force, the Criminal Investigation Department and other government departments. Meanwhile, the Anti-Rowdy Section of Kolkata Police has collected CCTV footage from the site of the incident. The Chief Minister said the footage would be examined and strict action would be taken against anyone found responsible for failing to manage the crowd. Mr. Adhikari asserted that no one responsible for the lapses would be spared. The Chorbagan community puja pandal has been closed, and the site has been handed over to forensic experts, the police Special Task Force and the Fire Brigade for investigation. The Chorbagan Durga Puja, which has grown in popularity in recent years, attracts large crowds. Meanwhile, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who is currently in Kolkata, is monitoring the situation and is in constant touch with the Chief Minister and other senior state officials. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said, all official programmes, including those involving the Union Home Minister, have been postponed in view of the tragedy. Mr Shah was scheduled to visit several Durga Puja pandals today. Union Home Minister said, he will visit the injured in the hospital today. The Chief Minister urged Durga Puja organisers, particularly those hosting elaborate theme-based celebrations, to ensure adequate lighting and sufficient entry and exit points to prevent overcrowding and ensure public safety. He stressed that human lives must take precedence over decorative themes, as organisers across Kolkata and other parts of West Bengal compete to create increasingly elaborate and attractive pandals.

national_raw_news.title: Kenya’s Charles Matata breaks course record to win men’s elite race at Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon 53 mins ago 34
national_raw_news.content: Kenya’s Charles Matata broke the course record to win the men’s elite race at the Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon today, while Ethiopia’s Wudinesh Alemu claimed the women’s title. Matata clocked 58 minutes, 52 seconds over the 21.097-kilometre course, shaving one second off the previous record set by Ethiopia’s Amedework Walelegn in 2020. Matata set the record to earn an additional 12,000 dollars on top of the 27,000 dollar winner’s prize. Kenya swept the men’s podium, with Samwel Nyamai Mailu finishing second in 59 minutes, 24 seconds and Stanley Waithaka Mburu third in 59 minutes, 33 seconds. Alemu won the women’s race in 1 hour, 6 minutes, 35 seconds. Kenya’s Selah Businei finished second in 1 hour, 7 minutes, 1 second, followed by Cynthia Chelangat Chepkwony in 1 hour, 7 minutes, 32 seconds. In the Indian elite men’s race, Shailesh Kushwaha won in one hour, five minutes and five seconds, ahead of Gaurav Mathur in one hour, five minutes and 11 seconds, and Hemant Kumar in one hour, five minutes and 37 seconds. Ankita Dhyani won the Indian elite women’s title in one hour, 12 minutes and 46 seconds. Soniya finished second in one hour, 14 minutes and 56 seconds, while Bhagirathi was third in one hour, 15 minutes and 51 seconds. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju, Chief of Defence Staff Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani and World Athletics Vice President Adille Sumariwalla attended the event. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta flagged off the Great Delhi Run.

national_raw_news.title: Captain Smit Machchhar reveals more details of the flydubai incident; says he hopes to return to ...
national_raw_news.content: Recovering well at Zayed Military Hospital in Abu Dhabi, Captain Smit Machchhar has given a detailed account of what he recalls from the day of the incident aboard flydubai flight FZ1073. In interviews with The National and Sky News Arabia, published on Friday evening, Captain Smit recounted how he was attacked by his co-pilot on the Dubai to Tel Aviv flight on 30th September. He has described the repeated blows, his attempts to get help, the cockpit door opening and shutting, and how he repeatedly lost consciousness as he fought to survive. Just before the attack, the other captain travelling as deadweight crew and who Captain Smit has described as a good friend, came into the cockpit and the two discussed their roasters, schedules, etc. Around this time, the co-pilot wanted took a toilet break even as the two captains continued their conversation. A few minutes into the conversation, the co-pilot said he wanted to pray. Accordingly, the other captain stepped out of the cockpit and the co-pilot started praying, positioned just behind Captain Smit. Captain Smit was seated, checking routine information like expected landing time on his computer, “And that’s when it started,” he said. He suddenly felt a very hard hit at the back of his head. The impact was so hard that he fell forward, almost falling on his control column and he thought there was something catastrophically wrong with the aircraft structure. But in the next couple of seconds, as the hits kept coming, he managed to glance back and realised what was going on. The person hitting him was his colleague in the cockpit, that he thought was supposed to be part of the team. Captain Smit said that his vision had become very narrow because of the blows, restricted to just a few inches and he could only see outlines. His immediate reaction was to guard himself from further hits. He quickly unbuckled his seatbelt, turned around and tried to block the blows. “And that’s when something flipped and I said, okay, I need to get some help in here,” he recalled. Captain Smit started screaming the other Captain’s name, tried to reach the switch to open the cockpit door and get help. Amid the screaming and everything going on, he lost consciousness for the first time, he said. He remembers being able to open the door, there was some shouting between the other captain and the co-pilot, and the door shut immediately after this. Barely staying conscious, Captain Smit heard the engine sounds going down and he felt the aircraft going into a dive. Having flown for a long time, Captain Smit said, he did not need the instruments to understand that the engines were spooling down and the aircraft was going down. Throughout this time, he was in and out of consciousness, he recalled. Smit said his memories of what happened next are still fragmented. But he remembers trying to reach the cockpit door. The next thing he remembers is lying face down between the cockpit and the galley, with the cockpit door open. He recalled a scene of panic, screaming and chaos. Several people were trying to control the situation in the cramped space around the cockpit entrance. Captain Smit said he was eventually pulled out of the cockpit and the senior cabin crew member reached him and helped him. Looking back, Smit said there was a moment when he thought he might not survive. “I told myself that, Smith, do something. You can’t die like this,” he said. He had not accepted his death, but realised he had to do something or he might not survive. It was the first time Captain Smit had met the co-pilot, and he said their interaction before the attack was usual and normal. He said there was nothing in their interaction that made him suspect anything was wrong. “It was the first time we met… there were some small talks… But nowhere till the point that anything would have caused me to think that, ‘Hey, hold on, there’s something off.’” Captain Smit also added that flying with new crew members was a routine part of the job and that the flight had started like...

national_raw_news.title: Truck crash near Sheetla Mata Temple in Gwalior kills 12, injures 39
national_raw_news.content: In Madhya Pradesh, twelve people were killed and 39 others injured after an out-of-control truck crashed into the outer wall of the Sheetla Mata Temple on Chinaur Road in Gwalior last night. The vehicle reportedly broke through police barricades, rolled down a steep slope and ploughed into devotees gathered on the road, crushing several pilgrims before coming to a halt. According to Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Dharmveer Singh Yadav, the accident occurred at around 1.30 AM when a truck loaded with paddy went out of control, hit devotees heading towards the Sheetla Mata Temple and crashed into the temple wall. The impact of the collision also caused the temple wall to collapse, triggering panic at the spot. Police and local residents rushed to the scene, rescued the injured and shifted them to nearby hospitals for treatment. Two police personnel who were on duty at the spot were also injured and are undergoing treatment in the hospital. President Droupadi Murmu and Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan have expressed condolences on the loss of life in a road accident in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. In a social media post, the President has prayed for the swift recovery of those injured. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also expressed grief at the mishap. Mr Modi has announced an ex-gratia of 2 lakh rupees from the Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund for the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives and fifty thousand rupees for those injured.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games 2026 to begin in Japan 6 hours ago 334
national_raw_news.content: The Asian Para Games 2026 will officially open at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan, today, with India aiming to build on its record medal haul at the previous edition. The fifth edition of the continental sporting event will bring together around three thousand athletes from 45 National Paralympic Committees. The Games will continue until 24th of October, with competitions across 18 sports. The opening ceremony today will be held at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya under the theme, “WABI: We Are Beautiful Individuals”. The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 2:30 PM Indian Standard Time. Several competitions, including blind football, para badminton, para table tennis and boccia, are scheduled to begin before the opening ceremony. Para-badminton player Pramod Bhagat and sprinter Simran Sharma will lead the Indian contingent as flag-bearers during the ceremony. Simran has replaced para-table tennis player Bhavina Patel to allow Patel adequate rest ahead of her quarter-final match tomorrow. India has fielded a 281-member contingent, comprising 168 athletes and 113 officials and support staff. The athletes include 112 men and 56 women, who will compete across 11 disciplines. The Indian squad features several prominent para-athletes, including javelin thrower Sumit Antil, para-badminton player Pramod Bhagat, para-shooter Avani Lekhara, para-archer Sheetal Devi, sprinter Simran Sharma and para-table tennis player Bhavina Patel. During the Asian Para Games 2023 at Hangzhou in China, India had secured a record 111 medals, comprising 29 gold, 31 silver and 51 bronze, to finish fifth in the overall standings. The tally surpassed India’s previous record of 72 medals at the 2018 edition in Jakarta. India will now look to build on that historic performance as the country’s para-athletes prepare to compete against the best talent from across Asia.

national_raw_news.title: Durga Puja celebrations continue across Odisha as devotees visit temples and pandals 10 mins ago 11
national_raw_news.content: Durga Puja celebrations have gripped Odisha, with devotees thronging temples and beautifully decorated puja pandals across the state. While Maha Ashtami rituals are being performed at ‘Shakti Peethas’, Maha Saptami Puja is underway at Durga Puja pandals, amid chants, devotional music and traditional festivities. Special security and traffic arrangements have been made in major towns and cities to ensure smooth darshan and the safe movement of devotees. The festive spirit of Durga Puja has reached a crescendo across Odisha, as thousands of devotees gather at temples and elaborately decorated pandals to offer prayers to Maa Durga. From the early morning hours, the air has resonated with devotional chants, the rhythmic beats of traditional drums and the sound of conch shells, creating an atmosphere of deep faith and spiritual fervour. While special Maha Ashtami rituals are being performed at ‘Shakti Peethas’ across the state, Maha Saptami Puja is underway at Durga Puja pandals, where priests are conducting traditional ceremonies and devotees are seeking the blessings of the Divine Mother. In Bhubaneswar and Cuttack, magnificent decorations, artistic installations and dazzling illuminations have added grandeur to the celebrations. Fairs and festive gatherings are also attracting people of all ages. Authorities have put special security and traffic arrangements in place at several locations to regulate crowds and facilitate smooth darshan. The festival, symbolising the triumph of good over evil, is bringing communities together in a celebration of devotion, tradition and the enduring spirit of Odisha.

national_raw_news.title: DRI seizes massive 137 kg consignment of crystal meth; busts coastal drug trafficking network
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Finance DRI seizes massive 137 kg consignment of crystal meth; busts coastal drug trafficking network; 4 arrested in Tamil Nadu Major intelligence-led operation foils suspected attempt to smuggle drug to Sri Lanka through maritime route Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 1:17PM by PIB Delhi In a major crackdown on organised drug trafficking, in one of the biggest narcotics seizures in Tamil Nadu’s coastal region in recent years , the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized 137 kg (gross) crystal methamphetamine, a banned synthetic drug, from a coastal village in Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu. Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers conducted an intensive surveillance and enforcement operation during 16–17 October 2026, successfully uncovering a suspected coastal drug-trafficking network attempting to smuggle the narcotic substances to Sri Lanka. The consignment was intended to be smuggled to Sri Lanka through mid-sea transfer. The value of the seized contraband in the illicit drug market is estimated to be in excess of Rs 100 crore. The operation followed specific intelligence indicating that a large consignment of narcotic substances had been transported to a coastal location in Nagapattinam district for storage and onward smuggling to Sri Lanka. A subsequent search led to the recovery of six duffel bags containing 27 silver-foil packets, with each weighing approximately 5 kg were recovered . The packets contained a white crystalline substance suspected to be methamphetamine of high purity. The contraband was seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. In a simultaneous search at the premises of the suspected organiser, DRI officers seized Rs. 10 lakh in cash suspected to represent sale proceeds . Two four-wheelers and one two-wheeler allegedly used for transporting the narcotic substance were also seized. The operation successfully exposed the drug trafficking network including persons involved in organising the coastal export, transportation, storage and logistics of the consignment. Four persons, have been arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and remanded to judicial custody. Through this operation, DRI has not only removed a significant quantity of contraband drugs from illicit circulation but also successfully dismantled a drug-trafficking network. This major seizure underscores DRI’s sustained efforts and enforcement capabilities in disrupting organised drug-trafficking networks and preventing the use of India’s coastline as a corridor for illicit narcotics trafficking. **** KT/KMN (Release ID: 2324872) Visitor Counter : 1176 Read this release in: Gujarati , Urdu , हिन्दी , Assamese , Tamil Share Ministry of Finance DRI seizes massive 137 kg consignment of crystal meth; busts coastal drug trafficking network; 4 arrested in Tamil Nadu Major intelligence-led operation foils suspected attempt to smuggle drug to Sri Lanka through maritime route Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 1:17PM by PIB Delhi In a major crackdown on organised drug trafficking, in one of the biggest narcotics seizures in Tamil Nadu’s coastal region in recent years , the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized 137 kg (gross) crystal methamphetamine, a banned synthetic drug, from a coastal village in Nagapattinam district,...

national_raw_news.title: DRI seizes 137 kg crystal meth worth over Rs 100 crore in Tamil Nadu, 4 arrested
national_raw_news.content: DRI seizes 137 kg crystal meth worth over Rs 100 crore in Tamil Nadu, 4 arrested Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर DRI seizes 137 kg crystal meth worth over Rs 100 crore in Tamil Nadu, 4 arrested ANI | Updated: Oct 18, 2026 15:10 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 18 (ANI): The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized 137 kg of crystal methamphetamine, valued at over Rs 100 crore in the illicit drug market, in Tamil Nadu's Nagapattinam district, busting a suspected coastal trafficking network allegedly attempting to smuggle the narcotic to Sri Lanka through a maritime route. Four persons have been arrested in connection with the seizure and remanded to judicial custody, the Ministry of Finance said in a statement on Sunday. The intelligence-led operation was conducted on October 16 and 17 following specific inputs that a large consignment of narcotic substances had been transported to a coastal village in Nagapattinam for storage and onwards smuggling to Sri Lanka through a mid-sea transfer. During the search, DRI officers recovered six duffel bags containing 27 silver-foil packets, each weighing approximately 5 kg. The packets contained a white crystalline substance suspected to be high-purity methamphetamine. The contraband, weighing 137 kg in gross, was seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. In a simultaneous search at the premises of the suspected organiser, officers also seized Rs 10 lakh in cash, believed to represent proceeds from drug sales. Two four-wheelers and a two-wheeler allegedly used to transport the narcotics were also seized during the operation. According to the Ministry, the investigation uncovered a network involving individuals allegedly responsible for organising the coastal export, transportation, storage and logistics of the consignment. The suspected trafficking operation was aimed at moving the narcotics out of India through a maritime route, with Sri Lanka identified as the intended destination. The seizure is among the major narcotics recoveries reported in Tamil Nadu's coastal region in recent years, highlighting enforcement efforts to prevent the country's coastline from being used as a corridor for illicit drug trafficking. The DRI said the operation removed a significant quantity of suspected contraband from circulation and disrupted the network involved in its movement. The agency continues to focus on intelligence-led enforcement against organised drug trafficking, including networks that use coastal locations and maritime transfers to facilitate the movement of narcotic substances.
